3372643_98d9d287.text: The intergeniculate leaflet (IGL) of the thalamus is a retinorecipient structure implicated in orchestrating circadian rhythmicity. The IGL network is highly GABAergic and consists mainly of neuropeptide Y‐synthesising and enkephalinergic neurons. A high density of GFAP‐immunoreactive astrocytes has been observed in the IGL, with a probable function in guarding neuronal inhibition. Interestingly, putatively enkephalinergic IGL neurons generate action potentials with an infra‐slow oscillatory (ISO) pattern in vivo in urethane anesthetised Wistar rats, under light‐on conditions only.
3372643_98d9d287.section: Anatomical location and structural organization of IGL neurons
